subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Memory Chips: SRAM, DRAM, and Flash
description: A fast breakdown of Memory Chips: SRAM, DRAM, and Flash for builders.

hook.text: Your phone stores photos, apps, and messages — all in chips made of transistors.

buildup.text: SRAM uses six transistors per bit. Fast but bulky — used for processor caches.

discovery.text: DRAM uses one transistor and one capacitor per bit. Dense and cheap — used for main memory.

twist.text: DRAM capacitors leak charge. The chip must refresh every bit thousands of times per second.

climax.text: Flash memory traps electrons in a floating gate. No refresh needed — data survives power-off.

punchline.text: Fast, dense, or persistent — each memory type trades one for the others.

quiz.question: Why does DRAM need constant refreshing?
options: Its transistors overheat without periodic cooling cycles
Its tiny capacitors leak charge, so stored bits must be rewritten constantly
The voltage supply fluctuates and must be re-calibrated
